Airtree adds A$5 million to Metacognition’s pre-seed

The pre-seed reaches A$15 million for robot reasoning, memory and navigation software.

Startup Daily ↗28 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

An extension of the existing round

Startup Daily reported on October 28 Australian time that Airtree invested another A$5 million in Adelaide-based Metacognition, following A$10 million a month earlier. The pre-seed totals A$15 million; it is not a separate additional A$15 million round.

Software for consequential tasks

Metacognition develops Zeos, navigation models, reasoning and memory tools. It aims to help agents and robots retain instructions, respond to emergencies and improve over time. Initial work includes simulations of open-cut mines and electricity grids controlled through verbal instructions.

Deployment evidence is still needed

The investment coincides with NavGPT-3, developed with collaborators and promoted as a strong language-navigation model. The report does not supply full benchmark results or deployed robot counts. Financing supports development rather than certifying reliability across tasks.
